questions.question: What is the AWS Shared Responsibility Model?
options: AWS manages each layer of the stack including data, IAM, and OS patching on EC2
Customers run security at each layer including the physical data centers and global network
AWS secures the cloud (hardware, hypervisor, facilities); customers secure what they put into it
AWS handles each compliance requirement on the customer's behalf with no customer involvement
questions.explanation: AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud (hardware, facilities, global infrastructure). Customers are responsible for security IN the cloud (data, IAM, OS patching on EC2, etc.).

questions.question: Which AWS service provides scalable object storage?
options: Amazon EBS
Amazon S3
Amazon EFS
Amazon EC2 Instance Store
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service) is AWS's object storage service. It stores data as objects in buckets, offers 99.999999999% (11 9s) durability.

questions.question: A startup wants the lowest latency to end-users in Tokyo, São Paulo, and Frankfurt. Which AWS architectural choice BEST addresses this?
options: Lower latency for nearby users plus data residency for regulatory compliance
Automatic synchronous replication of services across each Region as a default behavior
Identical published pricing across Regions so cost forecasting is fully predictable
Free inter-Region data transfer for any workload running multi-Region active-active
questions.explanation: Multi-Region with latency-based DNS sends each user to the geographically-closest healthy endpoint — the canonical "Regions exist to reduce latency" pattern. A single Region cannot beat the speed of light to three continents. Outposts extend AWS into customer datacenters; they don't solve global latency by themselves.

questions.question: Which EC2 pricing model offers the greatest discount for a long-term, steady-state workload?
options: On-Demand pricing per second
Spot Instances bidding on spare capacity
Reserved Instances with a 1- or 3-year commitment
Dedicated Hosts billed by the hour
questions.explanation: Reserved Instances with a 1 or 3-year commitment offer up to 72% discount vs On-Demand for predictable, steady-state workloads. Spot can be cheaper but can be interrupted.

questions.question: A media site serves 90% static assets (video, images) and sees viral traffic spikes from specific countries. Which AWS service combination MOST DIRECTLY reduces origin load and improves time-to-first-byte for those viewers?
options: A managed authoritative DNS service with health-checked routing policies
A managed site-to-site VPN service between on-premises and an AWS VPC
A Layer 7 load balancer that distributes traffic across EC2 target groups
A global Content Delivery Network that caches content at edge locations near users
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a CDN that distributes content from edge locations worldwide, reducing latency for end users by serving cached content from the nearest edge location.

questions.question: Which AWS service allows you to run code without provisioning servers?
options: Amazon EC2
Amazon ECS
Amazon LightSail
AWS Lambda
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service. You upload code and Lambda runs it in response to events. You pay only for execution time — no server management required.

questions.question: A developer needs to give an EC2 instance permission to read from one specific S3 bucket. Following AWS best practice, which approach should they use?
options: Identity and Access Management — who can do what in AWS
Internet Access Management — internet traffic
Infrastructure and Application Management — EC2 instances
Image and AMI Management — EC2 images
questions.explanation: IAM (Identity and Access Management) controls authentication (who you are) and authorization (what you can do) in AWS through users, groups, roles, and policies.

questions.question: What is an AWS Availability Zone (AZ)?
options: One or more discrete data centers with redundant power and networking inside a Region
A geographic Region such as us-east-1 that contains a number of Availability Zones
A globally distributed CloudFront edge location that caches content close to end users
A logically isolated network segment within a customer-owned VPC subnet boundary
questions.explanation: An AZ is one or more data centers within a Region with independent power, cooling, and networking. Multiple AZs in a Region enable high availability architecture.

questions.question: A regulated-industry customer running mission-critical workloads on AWS wants a named human on the AWS side: a Technical Account Manager who knows their architecture, reviews quarterly business reviews, and acts as their primary escalation. Which AWS Support plan includes a dedicated TAM by default?
options: Developer support — email-only support during business hours, no TAM
Enterprise support — includes a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM) and 15-minute critical-case response
Basic support — billing and account help only, no technical support, no TAM
Business support — 24×7 chat/phone/email and Trusted Advisor, but no dedicated TAM
questions.explanation: The Enterprise Support plan includes a dedicated TAM, concierge support, and 15-minute response time for business-critical issues. Business plan has < 1 hour response.

questions.question: What is the AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar that focuses on the ability to recover from failures?
options: Security
Reliability
Cost Optimization
Performance Efficiency
questions.explanation: The Reliability pillar of the Well-Architected Framework focuses on recovery from disruptions, dynamic resource acquisition, and mitigating misconfigurations.

questions.question: What is the purpose of AWS CloudTrail?
options: Captures EC2 instance CPU, memory, disk, and network performance metrics
Deploys and manages cloud infrastructure declaratively with YAML or JSON templates
Routes traffic between peered VPCs across Regions using a Transit Gateway hub
Records API calls and account activity across AWS services for security auditing
questions.explanation: CloudTrail records all API calls made to AWS services, providing an audit log of who did what, when, and from where. Essential for compliance and security investigations.

questions.question: A company runs a steady-state production workload on a fleet of m5.large EC2 instances 24/7 for the next 3 years. Which pricing model offers the LARGEST discount versus On-Demand?
options: A virtual machine running on the EC2 hypervisor in a customer-selected Region
AWS's global private backbone network connecting Regions and edge locations
A logically isolated virtual network in AWS with customer-defined IP ranges and subnets
A managed container orchestration platform built on Kubernetes for AWS workloads
questions.explanation: A VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) is a logically isolated virtual network in AWS. You control the IP range, subnets, route tables, and network gateways.

questions.question: What is the difference between horizontal and vertical scaling?
options: Horizontal means using bigger instances; vertical means launching more instances
Horizontal scaling applies to relational databases; vertical applies to compute fleets
Both terms describe the same scaling pattern and the choice depends on the workload
Horizontal means scaling out by adding instances; vertical means scaling up the size of one
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling (scale out/in) adds/removes instances. Vertical scaling (scale up/down) resizes the instance to a larger/smaller type. AWS Auto Scaling handles horizontal scaling.

questions.question: An architect needs to estimate the MONTHLY cost of a planned deployment (10 EC2 m6i.xlarge + 5 TB S3 Standard + 1 RDS db.m5.large + 100 GB data transfer) BEFORE provisioning anything. Which AWS tool produces a per-service estimate from the catalogue pricing?
options: AWS Cost Explorer — analyses ALREADY-incurred costs; no pre-deployment estimate
AWS Pricing Calculator — public web tool for estimating monthly cost from catalogue prices before deployment
AWS Budgets — alerts on real spend versus a threshold; doesn't estimate plans
AWS Trusted Advisor — best-practice recommendations on running infra, not pre-deploy pricing
questions.explanation: The AWS Pricing Calculator lets you estimate monthly costs for AWS services before you deploy them. Cost Explorer analyzes existing costs; Budgets sets alerts.

questions.question: What is AWS Auto Scaling?
options: Automatically swaps EC2 instance families to match a workload's CPU profile
Automatically applies operating system patches across a managed EC2 fleet
Automatically adjusts compute capacity by adding or removing instances based on demand
Automatically schedules backups for RDS databases and EBS volumes by tag
questions.explanation: AWS Auto Scaling monitors applications and automatically adjusts capacity (EC2 instances, ECS tasks, etc.) to maintain performance and minimize costs.

questions.question: A finance team is comparing cloud to traditional data-centre TCO. The AWS sales rep keeps using the phrase 'pay only for what you use'. The finance lead asks for a concrete definition in pricing terms. Which best describes this principle?
options: Consumption-based pricing — billing is per actual usage (per hour/second/GB/request), no upfront seat or hardware fee
Per-resource flat fee — charge regardless of usage, the data-centre licensing model
Flat monthly subscription — fixed monthly regardless of consumption
Upfront annual licensing — pay once for a year of access, the perpetual-software model
questions.explanation: One of the key cloud benefits: consumption-based pricing. Unlike on-premises infrastructure with fixed costs, cloud billing is based on actual consumption.

questions.question: Which AWS service is BEST suited to track who made an API call, when, from what IP address, and what parameters were used — for compliance auditing across an account?
options: AWS CloudTrail
AWS Inspector
AWS Config
Amazon CloudWatch
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch collects metrics (CPU, memory, disk, network), creates dashboards, and sends alarms when thresholds are breached. CloudTrail is for API auditing.

questions.question: What is an S3 bucket policy used for?
options: A JSON resource policy that controls access to an S3 bucket and its objects
A document that grants EC2 instance profile permissions to call AWS APIs
A rule set that defines lifecycle transitions between S3 storage classes
A configuration that enables server-side encryption defaults on objects
questions.explanation: S3 bucket policies are JSON-based resource policies that control who can access a bucket and what actions they can perform. They can grant access to other AWS accounts.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an Internet Gateway in a VPC?
options: Provides outbound and inbound internet access for resources in public subnets
Establishes a peered Layer 3 connection between two separate VPCs
Acts as a stateful firewall between subnets within the same VPC
Routes traffic between private subnets across multiple Availability Zones
questions.explanation: An Internet Gateway (IGW) is a horizontally-scaled, redundant VPC component that enables communication between VPC instances and the internet.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides infrastructure as code?
options: AWS Elastic Beanstalk
AWS OpsWorks
AWS CloudFormation
AWS Systems Manager
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation allows you to define AWS infrastructure as JSON or YAML templates and deploy it in a repeatable, automated way.

questions.question: What is Amazon Route 53?
options: A managed Layer 4 load balancing service for TCP and UDP
A Content Delivery Network that caches static assets at the edge
A managed site-to-site VPN service for hybrid connectivity
A scalable DNS and domain registration service with routing policies
questions.explanation: Route 53 is AWS's scalable DNS service. It routes users to applications, supports health checks, and offers routing policies like latency, geolocation, and failover.

questions.question: A team has medical imaging files that are accessed about 4× per year but, when accessed, must be retrievable in MILLISECONDS (not hours). They want to pay less than S3 Standard storage rates. Which S3 storage class fits?
options: S3 Standard-IA — same millisecond retrieval as Standard at a lower storage rate, with a per-GB retrieval fee — designed for infrequent access
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval — minutes-to-hours retrieval, cheaper but does not meet the millisecond requirement
S3 Standard — cheapest per retrieval but most expensive per GB stored, ill-suited for infrequent access
S3 Glacier Deep Archive — hours retrieval, cheapest storage, definitely not millisecond
questions.explanation: S3 Standard-IA is for data accessed less frequently but needs immediate access when required. Lower storage cost than S3 Standard but retrieval fee applies.

questions.question: What is the principle of least privilege in AWS IAM?
options: Grant users the minimum permissions required to perform their assigned tasks
Grant administrator access broadly so engineers can move quickly without friction
Use a single shared IAM user across the team for simpler credential management
Avoid IAM roles and rely on long-lived access keys attached to IAM users
questions.explanation: The principle of least privilege means granting only the permissions necessary to perform a task — nothing more. This minimizes the blast radius of compromised credentials.

questions.question: What is an EC2 Security Group?
options: A stateless packet filter that evaluates ordered allow and deny rules at the subnet boundary
A stateful instance-level firewall controlling inbound and outbound EC2 traffic with allow rules
An IAM-based group that controls which administrators can launch EC2 instances
A VPC route table entry that forwards specific destination CIDRs to a target gateway
questions.explanation: Security Groups are stateful (return traffic automatically allowed) instance-level firewalls. You define allow rules only — there are no deny rules. Compare with Network ACLs which are stateless and subnet-level.

questions.question: What is the difference between a Security Group and a Network ACL?
options: They behave identically; the difference is purely cosmetic in the AWS console UI
Security Groups: stateful, instance-level, allow-only. NACLs: stateless, subnet-level, allow and deny
Network ACLs apply at the EC2 instance level; Security Groups apply at the VPC subnet level
Security Groups are evaluated on outbound traffic; NACLs are evaluated on inbound traffic
questions.explanation: SG: stateful (return traffic auto-allowed), instance level, allow rules only, evaluated as a whole. NACL: stateless (return traffic needs explicit rule), subnet level, ordered allow/deny rules. instance-level, allow-only rules. Network ACLs: stateless, subnet-level, allow AND deny rules

questions.question: What is Amazon EBS?
options: Object storage similar to S3 with eleven nines of durability across an entire Region
Persistent block storage volumes for EC2 that outlive the instance and can be reattached
A POSIX file system that mounts to many EC2 instances across Availability Zones
Ephemeral instance store that is wiped when the EC2 instance stops or terminates
questions.explanation: EBS (Elastic Block Store) provides persistent block storage volumes attached to EC2. Unlike instance store, EBS persists after instance stop/terminate and can be detached/reattached.

questions.question: What is Amazon EFS?
options: An elastic NFS file system that multiple EC2 instances can mount simultaneously
A block storage volume that attaches to a single EC2 instance at a time
Object storage accessed over HTTPS using bucket and key naming
A tape-based archive tier with retrieval times measured in hours
questions.explanation: EFS (Elastic File System) is a managed NFS file system that can be mounted to multiple EC2 instances across Availability Zones simultaneously. Unlike EBS which attaches to one instance.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an AWS NAT Gateway?
options: Connects two VPCs together at Layer 3 with a peering relationship
Lets private subnet instances reach the internet outbound while staying unreachable inbound
Provides direct internet ingress and egress for instances in public subnets
Terminates IPsec VPN tunnels from on-premises networks into a VPC
questions.explanation: A NAT Gateway in a public subnet allows private subnet instances to reach the internet for updates/patches while remaining unreachable from inbound internet connections.

questions.question: A web tier has 6 EC2 instances serving HTTPS. A new release introduces autoscaling — at peak the fleet may grow to 30, at trough shrink to 3. The team needs a managed service that automatically registers/deregisters scaling instances and distributes inbound HTTPS requests with health checks. Which AWS service?
options: Amazon CloudFront — edge CDN for cached content, not a back-end load distributor
Amazon RDS read-replica — database scaling, not HTTPS distribution
Amazon Route 53 weighted records — DNS-level distribution, no per-request layer-7 health checking like ELB
Elastic Load Balancing — distributes inbound to EC2 / containers / IP / Lambda targets with health checks
questions.explanation: ELB distributes traffic across multiple targets. ALB (Application) = Layer 7/HTTP, NLB (Network) = Layer 4/TCP, GLB (Gateway) = Layer 3 for third-party appliances. Integrates with Auto Scaling.

questions.question: What is Amazon S3 Versioning?
options: A counter that records the creation order of S3 buckets in your account
Tracks revisions of bucket policies and ACLs over the lifetime of the bucket
Keeps multiple object versions to protect against accidental overwrite or deletion
Enables CloudTrail-style auditing of S3 GetObject and PutObject API calls per bucket
questions.explanation: S3 Versioning stores all versions of an object including writes and deletes. Enables recovery from accidental overwrites/deletes. Can be used with Lifecycle policies to manage costs.

questions.question: What is AWS Trusted Advisor?
options: An external penetration testing service that probes your public-facing endpoints
A static analyzer that grades IAM policies for over-permissive wildcards
A central place to manage organizational AWS accounts and consolidated billing
Real-time recommendations for cost, performance, security, fault tolerance, and limits
questions.explanation: Trusted Advisor inspects your AWS environment and provides actionable recommendations. Basic checks (free): S3 bucket permissions, MFA on root account. Full checks require Business or Enterprise support.

questions.question: What is the AWS Free Tier?
options: Every AWS service is offered free of charge for accounts under a usage cap
The free tier covers EC2 only and excludes storage, networking, and other services
Limited free usage for 12 months on new accounts plus always-free and short trial offers
Startup credits granted to qualified companies through the AWS Activate program
questions.explanation: AWS Free Tier includes: 12-month free (new accounts) — e.g., 750hr/month EC2 t2.micro; Always free — e.g., 1M Lambda requests/month; Trial — e.g., 2 months Amazon Redshift.

questions.question: A team needs a managed relational database with: (a) MySQL/PostgreSQL wire-compatibility (zero application change), (b) auto-scaling storage up to 128 TB, (c) up to 15 low-latency cross-AZ read replicas, (d) standard AWS billing per second. Which managed RDS engine fits ALL four?
options: DynamoDB — NoSQL key-value, NOT MySQL/PostgreSQL wire-compatible
ElastiCache for Redis — in-memory key-value, not a relational engine
Amazon Aurora (MySQL- or PostgreSQL-compatible) — managed RDBMS with auto-scaling storage and up to 15 replicas
Redshift — columnar data warehouse for analytics, not OLTP RDBMS
questions.explanation: Aurora is AWS's cloud-native relational database. It auto-scales storage, replicates across 3 AZs with 6 copies, and offers serverless options. Fully managed within RDS.

questions.question: What is AWS IAM Role?
options: A named IAM principal with long-lived access keys for programmatic access
An assumable IAM identity with permissions and short-lived credentials via STS
A container that aggregates IAM users to share a common set of permissions
A JSON document that describes one or more allowed or denied API actions
questions.explanation: IAM Roles are assumable identities with permissions. EC2 instances, Lambda functions, and cross-account users assume roles. No static credentials — uses temporary security tokens via STS.

questions.question: What is Amazon SQS?
options: A real-time streaming service that ingests and processes shard-partitioned events
A workflow orchestration service that coordinates AWS services as state machines
A pub/sub notification service that fans messages out to many subscribers at once
A managed message queue that decouples components by buffering messages until processed
questions.explanation: SQS (Simple Queue Service) decouples microservices by providing a durable message buffer. Producers send messages; consumers poll and process them. Prevents data loss if a consumer fails.

questions.question: What is the difference between SQS and SNS?
options: They are functionally identical and either may be used interchangeably for messaging
SNS retains messages durably while SQS forwards messages without storing them
SQS is a pull-based queue for decoupling; SNS is a push-based pub/sub for fan-out
SQS is purpose-built for outbound email while SNS is for application queuing
questions.explanation: SQS: one consumer polls messages from a queue (point-to-point). SNS (Simple Notification Service): one message fan-out to multiple subscribers (email, SQS, Lambda, HTTP) simultaneously.

questions.question: What is AWS Snowball?
options: A managed disaster recovery service that orchestrates failover to a secondary Region
A cold object storage class with retrieval times measured in hours
A CloudFront edge location that caches content close to end users
A physical appliance for offline transfer of large datasets to or from AWS storage
questions.explanation: AWS Snowball is a secure, physical appliance for offline data migration. 80TB capacity. Snowball Edge adds compute. Snowmobile is a 100PB truck for exabyte migrations.

questions.question: What is AWS Elastic Beanstalk?
options: A managed Kubernetes control plane that runs upstream Kubernetes clusters
A managed Docker container registry that stores and serves OCI images
An infrastructure-as-code tool that synthesizes templates from imperative code
A PaaS that handles capacity, load balancing, scaling, and health for deployed apps
questions.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk is a PaaS that deploys web apps (Java, .NET, PHP, Node.js, Python, Ruby, Go, Docker). You upload code; Beanstalk handles the infrastructure. You still control the underlying resources.

questions.question: What does the 'S' in HTTPS stand for, and which AWS service helps implement it?
options: Security — AWS Shield Advanced protects against volumetric DDoS attacks at the edge
Standard — AWS WAF inspects HTTP requests against managed rule groups for OWASP risks
Speed — AWS Global Accelerator routes users over the AWS private global backbone
Secure — AWS Certificate Manager issues free public TLS certificates for ALB and CloudFront
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses TLS/SSL for encryption. AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) provisions and manages free public SSL/TLS certificates for use with ELB, CloudFront, and API Gateway.

questions.question: What is Amazon Redshift?
options: A managed in-memory cache compatible with Redis and Memcached protocols
A relational database optimized for OLTP workloads with multi-AZ failover
A petabyte-scale managed data warehouse using columnar storage and MPP for analytics
A NoSQL time-series database tuned for IoT sensor and metrics ingestion
questions.explanation: Redshift is AWS's managed data warehouse for analytics (OLAP). Uses columnar storage and MPP (Massively Parallel Processing) to run complex analytical queries across petabytes of data.

questions.question: What is AWS Config?
options: Manages application and OS configuration drift on running EC2 fleets at scale
Records and evaluates AWS resource configurations over time for compliance and audit
Deploys application code to EC2, on-premises servers, and Lambda functions
Authors, attaches, and audits IAM identity-based and resource-based policies
questions.explanation: AWS Config continuously records resource configurations and relationships, enabling: compliance checking against rules, change history tracking, and troubleshooting configuration drift.

questions.question: A public-facing web tier is hit with a sustained Layer-3/4 volumetric DDoS (SYN floods, UDP reflection). The customer wants automatic, no-config-required L3/L4 DDoS protection AT NO ADDITIONAL CHARGE; for the higher tier (cost-protection guarantees, DDoS Response Team access) they're willing to pay extra. Which service provides this?
options: AWS Shield (Standard = free, Advanced = paid) — L3/L4 DDoS protection with the cost-protection tier described
AWS WAF — Layer-7 HTTP rules, not L3/L4 volumetric protection
AWS KMS — key management, unrelated to DDoS
AWS Certificate Manager — TLS-cert lifecycle, unrelated to DDoS
questions.explanation: AWS Shield Standard: free, automatic DDoS protection for all AWS customers. Shield Advanced: paid, enhanced protection for EC2, ELB, CloudFront, Route 53 with the DDoS Response Team (DRT) and financial protection.

questions.question: What is Amazon Kinesis used for?
options: A managed relational database engine with read replicas and Multi-AZ failover
Real-time streaming data ingestion, processing, and analytics for high-volume sources
Object storage for files of any size with eleven nines of durability
A managed message queue that buffers work between decoupled microservices
questions.explanation: Kinesis enables real-time processing of streaming data: Kinesis Data Streams (ingest), Kinesis Data Firehose (load to S3/Redshift), Kinesis Data Analytics (SQL on streams), Kinesis Video Streams. processing, and analytics at scale

questions.question: What is AWS WAF?
options: A managed site-to-site or client VPN service for hybrid network connectivity
An intrusion detection system that uses ML to flag suspicious VPC Flow Logs
A network firewall that filters Layer 3 and Layer 4 traffic at VPC boundaries
A web application firewall that filters HTTP requests for SQLi, XSS, and bad actors
questions.explanation: AWS WAF filters web traffic to CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, and AppSync. You create rules to allow/block requests based on IP, headers, body content, or SQL/XSS patterns.

questions.question: What is Amazon ElastiCache?
options: A managed disk-based relational database with automated patching and backups
A managed in-memory cache (Redis or Memcached) for sub-millisecond reads and offload
A CDN edge cache that stores web assets close to end users globally
An accelerator that caches frequently read S3 objects in front of the bucket
questions.explanation: ElastiCache reduces database load by caching frequent queries in memory. Redis supports persistence, pub/sub, sorted sets. Memcached is simpler, multi-threaded. Both offer microsecond read latency.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides serverless container execution?
options: Amazon EKS managed Kubernetes control plane
Amazon ECS using the EC2 launch type with self-managed instances
AWS Fargate serverless compute engine for containers
AWS Lambda function runtime for event-driven code
questions.explanation: AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers (used with ECS or EKS). No EC2 instances to manage — you define CPU/memory requirements, and AWS handles the infrastructure.

questions.question: What is the AWS Global Accelerator?
options: A globally distributed CDN that caches static and dynamic content at the edge
A managed authoritative DNS service with latency-based and weighted routing
Routes user traffic over the AWS global backbone to the closest healthy regional endpoint
A regional Layer 7 load balancer that distributes HTTP traffic across targets
questions.explanation: Global Accelerator uses AWS's private global network (not the internet) to route traffic to the optimal regional endpoint, reducing latency and improving failover for global applications.

questions.question: What is the difference between Multi-AZ and Read Replicas in RDS?
options: Multi-AZ and Read Replicas serve the same purpose and are functionally interchangeable
Read Replicas exist to provide point-in-time backups of the primary database engine
Multi-AZ: synchronous standby for HA failover. Read Replicas: asynchronous copies for read scaling
Multi-AZ is intended for cross-Region disaster recovery rather than in-Region HA failover
questions.explanation: Multi-AZ: synchronous standby in different AZ for failover HA — automatic failover ~1-2min. Read Replicas: asynchronous copies for read scaling — promotes manually for DR. Both can exist simultaneously.

questions.question: What is AWS Artifact?
options: A managed source code repository for Git-based version control of application code
A container image registry that stores and serves OCI images for ECS and EKS
A self-service portal for AWS compliance reports such as SOC, PCI DSS, and ISO 27001
A managed continuous integration build service that compiles and tests source code
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact provides on-demand access to AWS's compliance documentation: SOC 1/2/3, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, HIPAA reports, and agreements. Useful for enterprise compliance and audits.

questions.question: What is Amazon Macie?
options: An intelligent threat detection service that analyzes VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs
A managed firewall that filters Layer 3 and Layer 4 traffic at VPC boundaries
A managed data security service that uses ML to find sensitive data such as PII in S3
A centralized key management service for creating and rotating encryption keys
questions.explanation: Macie uses machine learning to automatically discover and protect sensitive data (PII, financial data) in S3 buckets, identifying overly permissive access or sensitive data exposure.

questions.question: What is Amazon GuardDuty?
options: A managed web application firewall that inspects HTTP requests against rule groups
An endpoint antivirus agent installed on EC2 instances for malware scanning
A network intrusion detection appliance deployed inline at the VPC boundary
A managed threat detection service that analyzes VPC Flow Logs, CloudTrail, and DNS logs
questions.explanation: GuardDuty uses ML and threat intelligence to detect unusual API calls, unauthorized deployments, cryptocurrency mining, and compromised instances — with no agents to install.

questions.question: What is AWS Cost Explorer?
options: A pricing calculator for estimating future spend on workloads not yet deployed
A configuration page where you set spend alerts and trigger automated actions
A tool to visualize and analyze actual AWS cost and usage with granular filtering
A compliance portal that surfaces SOC, PCI, and ISO reports for your accounts
questions.explanation: Cost Explorer lets you analyze historical cost trends, identify cost drivers, forecast future spend, and find optimization opportunities with detailed filtering and charting.

questions.question: What is AWS Organizations?
options: A managed directory of IAM users with built-in single sign-on for the AWS Console
A project management portal for tracking AWS migration and modernization initiatives
Central management of multiple AWS accounts with consolidated billing, SCPs, and OUs
A console where you build and manage Auto Scaling groups for EC2 instances
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations enables centralized management of multiple AWS accounts: consolidated billing (volume discounts), Service Control Policies to restrict account permissions, and account grouping in OUs.

questions.question: What is a Service Control Policy (SCP) in AWS Organizations?
options: An IAM identity-based policy attached directly to users, groups, and roles
A guardrail that caps the maximum permissions for accounts in an Organization unit
A VPC-level network policy that filters traffic between subnets and gateways
A CloudFormation template that provisions standardized infrastructure stacks
questions.explanation: SCPs are guardrails. They don't grant permissions but define the maximum allowable permissions for accounts in OUs. Even if an IAM policy allows an action, an SCP restriction takes precedence.

questions.question: What is the AWS Marketplace?
options: A digital catalog of third-party software, AMIs, and SaaS products with flexible billing
An online catalog where AWS sells branded physical hardware appliances
An internal AWS career site listing technical and non-technical job openings
A marketplace for buying, selling, and trading Reserved Instance capacity
questions.explanation: AWS Marketplace lets customers find, subscribe to, and deploy third-party software that runs on AWS. Includes security, networking, data, ML, and business intelligence tools with flexible billing.

questions.question: What does 'elasticity' mean in cloud computing?
options: Manually stretching the physical capacity of on-premises hardware over time
The ability to automatically scale resources up and down with demand and pay for actual use
A long-horizon capacity planning exercise done annually by infrastructure teams
A static, fixed allocation of resources reserved for an application's peak load
questions.explanation: Elasticity means automatically growing (scale out) and shrinking (scale in) resources based on real-time demand. AWS Auto Scaling provides elasticity for EC2, ECS, DynamoDB, and other services.

questions.question: What is Amazon Inspector?
options: A cost analysis tool that breaks down spend by service, account, tag, and Region
A configuration management tool that records and evaluates resource state over time
A compliance reporting tool that maps controls to SOC, PCI, and ISO frameworks
An automated security assessment of EC2 and Lambda for CVEs and unintended exposure
questions.explanation: Amazon Inspector automatically scans for known CVEs in running EC2/Lambda workloads and checks for unintended network accessibility (e.g., open SSH to 0.0.0.0/0), providing prioritized findings.

questions.question: An auditor asks AWS who is responsible for: (1) the physical security of the data centre, (2) hypervisor patching, (3) the customer's EC2 guest OS patching, (4) the customer's application data encryption. Which mapping is correct under the Shared Responsibility Model?
options: Customer owns ALL four items — incorrect, AWS owns the foundation
AWS owns ALL four items — incorrect, customer owns IN-cloud responsibilities
Mapping varies by support tier — incorrect, the model is fixed, not support-tier-dependent
AWS = security OF the cloud (DC, hardware, hypervisor, network); Customer = security IN the cloud (guest OS, IAM, data, application config)
questions.explanation: AWS: physical security, data center facilities, networking hardware, hypervisor, and managed service infrastructure. Customer: everything they put in the cloud — data encryption, IAM, OS patching on EC2, network config.

questions.question: What is Amazon CloudWatch Logs?
options: Centralized log collection and analysis for AWS services, EC2, Lambda, and on-premises sources
A managed database that stores structured application data with SQL access
A Git-based version control service for application source code and infrastructure
A log shipper specifically for S3 server access logs and CloudFront access logs
questions.explanation: CloudWatch Logs centralizes logs from any source. You can create metric filters (count errors in logs), set alarms, and analyze with CloudWatch Logs Insights queries.

questions.question: What is the difference between Availability Zones and Regions in AWS?
options: Availability Zones and Regions are interchangeable terms in the AWS documentation
AZs are global resources visible everywhere; Regions are scoped to a single facility location
A Region is a geographic area with three or more AZs; an AZ is one or more isolated data centers
Regions hold object storage exclusively while AZs are reserved for compute workloads alone
questions.explanation: A Region (e.g., us-east-1) is a geographic cluster of AZs. An AZ (e.g., us-east-1a) is one or more data centers with independent infrastructure. Multi-AZ deployments protect against single data center failure.

questions.question: What is Amazon API Gateway?
options: A physical network gateway device that bridges on-premises and AWS networks
A globally distributed CDN that caches API responses at edge locations near users
A managed authoritative DNS service with health-checked routing policies for APIs
A managed service for creating, publishing, and securing REST and WebSocket APIs at scale
questions.explanation: API Gateway is the front door for backend services (Lambda, EC2, HTTP endpoints). It handles authentication, throttling, caching, monitoring, versioning, and API key management.

questions.question: What is AWS Step Functions?
options: A continuous integration and delivery pipeline that builds, tests, and deploys code
A schema-conversion and data-migration service for moving on-premises databases
A managed batch processing service that schedules and runs large-scale compute jobs
A serverless orchestration service that coordinates AWS services as visual state machines
questions.explanation: Step Functions orchestrates distributed applications as state machines with visual workflows. Coordinates Lambda, ECS, DynamoDB, SNS, SQS, and more with built-in error handling and retries.

questions.question: Which of the following is an AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar focused on reducing costs?
options: Operational Excellence
Cost Optimization
Reliability
Performance Efficiency
questions.explanation: Cost Optimization pillar focuses on avoiding unnecessary costs: right-sizing instances, using Reserved/Spot pricing, deleting unused resources, and understanding spend. All 6 pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability.

questions.question: What is AWS Secrets Manager?
options: A consumer password manager service for end users to store browser credentials
An S3-level service that automatically encrypts new objects with customer-managed keys
A configurable IAM password policy that enforces length and complexity for IAM users
Stores and rotates secrets like API keys, DB credentials, and tokens with KMS encryption
questions.explanation: Secrets Manager stores secrets securely and can automatically rotate them (e.g., RDS passwords every 30 days) without application downtime. Applications retrieve secrets via API — no hardcoded credentials.

questions.question: An architect new to AWS asks where to find AWS's prescriptive best-practice guidance, organised into pillars that an architecture review can score against (with detailed lenses for serverless, machine-learning, SaaS, IoT). Which official AWS resource is this?
options: Well-Architected Framework — best-practice guidance across the 6 pillars (Operations, Security, Reliability, Performance, Cost, Sustainability) plus lenses
AWS Pricing Catalogue — public price list, not best practices
AWS Certification Blueprint — exam-prep guide, not a design framework
AWS Solution Architect Deployment Checklist — there is no such named official artefact
questions.explanation: The Well-Architected Framework helps architects build secure, high-performing, resilient, and efficient infrastructure. Use the Well-Architected Tool in the AWS console for free architectural reviews.

questions.question: What is Amazon Athena?
options: A managed transactional database engine that supports MySQL and PostgreSQL APIs
A serverless interactive query service that runs ANSI SQL directly against S3 data
A managed data migration service for moving on-premises databases to AWS RDS
A managed ETL service that prepares and transforms data for downstream analytics
questions.explanation: Athena queries CSV, JSON, Parquet, ORC data directly in S3 using SQL. No loading required. Pay per TB scanned. Use Parquet format and partitioning to reduce costs. Integrates with AWS Glue Data Catalog.

questions.question: What is AWS Glue?
options: A network performance monitoring service that pings VPC and on-premises endpoints
A continuous integration and delivery service that automates application deployments
A serverless ETL service for preparing and loading data, with a metadata Data Catalog
A real-time data streaming service that ingests events into shard-partitioned streams
questions.explanation: AWS Glue provides: Data Catalog (metadata repository for all your data sources), ETL jobs (serverless Spark-based transformations), and Crawlers (auto-discover schema from S3, RDS, etc.).

questions.question: What is Amazon ECS (Elastic Container Service)?
options: A managed container orchestrator that runs Docker tasks on EC2 instances or Fargate
A managed virtual machine service that schedules and migrates EC2 workloads automatically
A managed container image registry that stores and serves OCI images privately
A managed Kubernetes control plane that runs upstream-compatible Kubernetes clusters
questions.explanation: ECS manages containerized applications. EC2 launch type: you manage the underlying EC2 fleet. Fargate: serverless — no EC2 management. Amazon ECR stores container images. ECS integrates with ALB, IAM, CloudWatch.

questions.question: What is an AMI (Amazon Machine Image)?
options: A web management console for monitoring and operating AWS resources from a browser
A template containing OS, applications, and configuration used to launch EC2 instances
An asymmetric encryption key used to sign and verify EC2 launch parameters
A networking template that defines a VPC's subnets, route tables, and gateways
questions.explanation: AMIs include: OS, pre-installed software, EBS snapshot mappings, and permissions. You can create custom AMIs from running instances for rapid deployment (Golden AMI pattern). AMIs are region-specific. application server, and application configuration used to launch EC2 instances — enables rapid, consistent instance deployment

questions.question: What is AWS CloudTrail?
options: A network performance monitor that measures latency and packet loss inside a VPC
Records every AWS API call (who, what, when, from where) for security and audit
A general-purpose log aggregation service that ingests application logs from any source
A traffic flow analyzer that captures packet samples from VPC interfaces for inspection
questions.explanation: CloudTrail logs every API call: Console actions, CLI commands, SDK calls, service-to-service calls. Stores in S3. Essential for security investigations: 'who deleted that S3 bucket? when did that IAM policy change?'

questions.question: What is the difference between AWS CloudFormation and CDK?
options: CloudFormation and CDK are interchangeable names for the same underlying AWS service
CloudFormation uses YAML or JSON templates; CDK uses programming languages that synthesize CFN
CDK is restricted to container deployments while CloudFormation handles other resource types
CloudFormation has been deprecated and CDK is the supported AWS IaC tool going forward
questions.explanation: CloudFormation is the foundational IaC service — template-based. CDK allows writing infrastructure using familiar languages with OOP constructs, then synthesizes CloudFormation. Higher level of abstraction.

questions.question: What is an IAM Policy Evaluation — what happens when Allow and Deny exist?
options: An explicit Allow takes precedence over an explicit Deny when both apply to the same action
Evaluation depends on the order in which IAM policies were attached to the principal
Whichever statement is more specific in resource, condition, or action wins regardless of effect
An explicit Deny overrides any Allow; with no matching statement the request is implicitly denied
questions.explanation: AWS IAM policy evaluation: Any explicit Deny wins regardless of any Allow. This enables denying specific actions even for admins. All requests start as implicitly denied — Allows must be explicitly granted.

questions.question: What is AWS Direct Connect?
options: A managed site-to-site VPN that tunnels encrypted IPsec traffic over the internet
A peering arrangement between AWS and CDN providers for cached content delivery
A managed internet transit service that peers with multiple Tier-1 carriers for AWS
A dedicated physical link between on-premises and AWS bypassing the public internet
questions.explanation: Direct Connect provides 1Gbps or 10Gbps dedicated connections via AWS Direct Connect Partners. Unlike VPN, no internet fluctuations. Good for large data transfers, hybrid cloud, and compliance requirements.

questions.question: What is AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store?
options: A managed secret rotation service that schedules KMS-backed credential rotations
A bucket-level service for storing and reading S3 configuration files at scale
An EC2 fleet management console for patching, inventory, and remote command execution
Hierarchical config and secret storage with SecureString KMS encryption and a free standard tier
questions.explanation: Parameter Store stores config data (DB strings, feature flags, AMI IDs) hierarchically (e.g., /prod/db/password). Free for standard parameters. SecureString type encrypts with KMS. Alternative to hardcoded config.

questions.question: What is Amazon DynamoDB and when should you use it?
options: A managed relational database optimized for OLAP analytical workloads at petabyte scale
A columnar data warehouse engine designed for complex analytical SQL across petabytes
A serverless NoSQL key-value and document database with single-digit millisecond latency
A graph database engine that supports property graphs and the openCypher query language
questions.explanation: DynamoDB: zero administration, auto-scales from 0 to millions of requests/second. Single-digit millisecond latency. Choose when: high throughput, flexible schema, simple queries by primary key. Not ideal for complex joins.

questions.question: What is AWS Lambda cold start?
options: A configuration delay that occurs the first time a function is deployed into a new Region
A billing calculation that adds an extra charge for the first invocation each calendar day
Latency to provision a new execution environment, load runtime, and initialize code (~100ms–1s)
A timeout event raised when function execution exceeds the configured maximum duration
questions.explanation: Lambda cold start = time to provision container + load runtime + init your code. Mitigation: Provisioned Concurrency (keeps environments warm), Lambda SnapStart (Java), smaller deployment packages, faster runtimes (Node/Python vs Java).

questions.question: A network team is connecting 10 VPCs. With VPC Peering each pair needs its own peer (a full mesh = 45 peerings) AND traffic is not transitive (A→B→C does not work via two peerings). With one alternative service the team creates one hub and N spoke attachments, with transitive routing between any spokes. Which two services and which difference?
options: VPC Peering and Transit Gateway are interchangeable — false, the model is different
Transit Gateway is the legacy product; VPC Peering replaced it — false, opposite
VPC Peering = 1:1 non-transitive; Transit Gateway = hub-and-spoke with TRANSITIVE routing between attachments
VPC Peering supports more attachments than Transit Gateway — false, TGW supports many more
questions.explanation: VPC Peering: simple, low-cost, no transitive routing (A↔B and B↔C doesn't mean A↔C). Transit Gateway: scalable hub for 1000s of VPCs and VPNs with transitive routing, route tables, and multicast support.

questions.question: What S3 storage class should you use for data accessed less than once per year?
options: S3 Glacier Deep Archive for long-term archival with multi-hour retrieval and the lowest cost per GB
S3 Standard for frequently accessed objects with millisecond first-byte latency
S3 Intelligent-Tiering with automatic movement between frequent and infrequent access tiers
S3 One Zone-IA for infrequent access in a single AZ at lower cost than Standard-IA
questions.explanation: S3 storage classes by access frequency: Standard > Intelligent-Tiering > Standard-IA > One Zone-IA > Glacier Instant > Glacier Flexible Retrieval > Glacier Deep Archive. Match access pattern to class to minimize costs.

questions.question: An operations engineer wants to scale capacity based on demand for: (a) EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling Group, (b) DynamoDB read/write capacity, (c) ECS service desired-count, (d) Aurora read replicas. AWS offers a unified service that orchestrates scaling across all of these. Which?
options: Scaling only available for EC2 — false; multiple services scale
AWS Compute Optimizer — recommends right-sizing, doesn't perform autoscale
Elastic Load Balancing — distributes traffic, not capacity scaling
AWS Auto Scaling — orchestrates dynamic scaling across EC2 ASG, DynamoDB, ECS, Aurora replicas via target-tracking and step policies
questions.explanation: Auto Scaling policies: Target Tracking (e.g., CPU at 70%), Step Scaling (add 2 instances when CPU > 80%), Scheduled Scaling (predict load). Scaling out = add instances, Scaling in = remove instances.

questions.question: What is IAM Access Analyzer?
options: A password auditing tool that flags weak or reused IAM user passwords for rotation
A wizard-style IAM policy generator that builds documents from CloudTrail history
Analyzes resource policies and roles to identify resources shared with external principals
A cost analysis tool that attributes spend to resources, accounts, tags, and services
questions.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer uses automated reasoning to find S3 buckets, KMS keys, Lambda functions, IAM roles, and SQS queues that are accessible from outside your AWS account — reducing data exposure risk.

questions.question: What is the purpose of AWS PrivateLink?
options: A managed client and site-to-site VPN service for secure remote access into a VPC
A bucket-level S3 feature that creates named access points with distinct IAM policies
Private connectivity between VPCs and AWS or partner services without crossing the public internet
An add-on feature of Direct Connect that establishes virtual interfaces in a VPC
questions.explanation: PrivateLink creates private endpoints in your VPC for AWS services (S3, DynamoDB, CloudWatch) or third-party SaaS services. Traffic stays on AWS network — no internet exposure, no NAT gateway costs for AWS service traffic.

questions.question: What is AWS Budgets?
options: A real-time billing dashboard that displays current month-to-date charges by service
A cost analysis tool that visualizes historical spend trends across services and tags
Custom cost and usage budgets with alerts and optional automated actions on threshold breach
A console for managing Reserved Instance and Savings Plans purchases and modifications
questions.explanation: AWS Budgets lets you define cost/usage/RI coverage budgets with SNS email/SMS alerts. Budget Actions can automatically apply IAM policies or stop EC2/RDS instances when thresholds are crossed.

questions.question: A global service needs DNS routing that, on a per-record basis, can: route by latency to closest Region, fail over from primary to secondary on health-check fail, weight requests across blue/green deployments, geofence answers by user country, and return multiple answers with health-aware selection. Which AWS DNS service provides ALL of these routing policies?
options: Route 53 supports a single simple round-robin policy — false; many policies exist
Route 53 routing policies apply only to Alias records — false; they apply to A, AAAA, CNAME, Alias
Route 53 supports: Simple, Weighted, Latency-based, Failover, Geolocation, Geoproximity, Multivalue-Answer, IP-based
Route 53 routing is scoped to EC2 — false; targets can be any IP
questions.explanation: Route 53 routing policies enable sophisticated DNS-based traffic management: Weighted for canary deployments, Latency-based for global performance, Failover for disaster recovery, Geolocation for compliance/localization.

questions.question: What is the difference between AWS Managed Policies and Customer Managed Policies?
options: AWS Managed are pre-built and AWS-maintained; Customer Managed are authored and maintained by you
AWS Managed Policies and Customer Managed Policies behave identically at evaluation time
Customer Managed Policies are inherently less secure than AWS Managed Policies by design
AWS Managed Policies attach to IAM users and groups but are blocked from attaching to roles
questions.explanation: AWS Managed Policies: maintained by AWS, updated automatically when services change, reusable. Customer Managed: you control content, version history, can apply fine-grained permissions. Inline policies: embedded in a single identity.

questions.question: What is Amazon CloudFront?
options: A specialized CDN built specifically for video streaming and live broadcast workflows
A web application firewall that filters Layer 7 HTTP requests against managed rules
A managed authoritative DNS service for routing users to the closest healthy endpoint
A global CDN with hundreds of edge locations caching content close to end users
questions.explanation: CloudFront caches static and dynamic content at edge locations. Reduces origin load and latency for global users. Supports Lambda@Edge for edge compute, signed URLs/cookies for private content, and AWS WAF integration.

questions.question: What is the AWS Pricing Calculator?
options: A real-time billing tool that displays current month-to-date charges across services
An invoice management portal for downloading and paying outstanding AWS invoices
A monthly cost savings report comparing actual spend to a defined budget baseline
A free web tool to estimate monthly costs for proposed AWS architectures before deployment
questions.explanation: The AWS Pricing Calculator (calculator.aws.amazon.com) helps estimate costs upfront. Model EC2 instance types, storage, data transfer, and other services to build a cost estimate for budget approval or comparison.

questions.question: What is AWS Support Plans and what do they include?
options: Four tiers: Basic (free), Developer, Business, and Enterprise — each adding response speed and channels
Every AWS Support plan provides 24/7 phone support and a Technical Account Manager
Each Support plan includes a dedicated Technical Account Manager regardless of tier
Enterprise Support is included free with any AWS account that has spend above a threshold
questions.explanation: Support plan tiers: Basic (free) → Developer → Business → Enterprise On-Ramp → Enterprise. Business and above get: 24/7 phone support, full Trusted Advisor checks, and access to Infrastructure Event Management.

questions.question: What is Amazon SES (Simple Email Service)?
options: A monitoring service that collects metrics, logs, and traces from AWS workloads
A spam filter and content classification service for inbound email traffic
A cloud email service for sending transactional, marketing, and notification emails at scale
A desktop email client for managing AWS root and IAM user account communications
questions.explanation: SES sends emails from applications (order confirmations, password resets, newsletters). Integrates with Lambda and SNS. Handles bounce/complaint processing. Can also receive emails and trigger Lambda functions.

questions.question: What is the Principle of Least Privilege in AWS?
options: Grant administrator permissions broadly so engineers do not hit permission errors at runtime
Grant broad read access permissions to each IAM user across the organization by default
Grant the minimum permissions required, start with none, add as needed, and audit regularly
Apply the principle to IAM users and exempt IAM roles from the same level of scrutiny
questions.explanation: Least privilege: users, roles, and services should have only the exact permissions they need. Use IAM Access Advisor to see last used permissions. Remove unused permissions. Prefer managed policies over wildcard (*) actions.

questions.question: What is Amazon FSx?
options: A new EBS volume type optimized for high-throughput, low-latency database workloads
Managed file systems including FSx for Windows, Lustre, NetApp ONTAP, and OpenZFS
A managed file service that exposes NFS shares and competes directly with EFS pricing
A managed gateway that exposes S3 buckets as on-premises file shares to clients
questions.explanation: FSx provides purpose-built managed file systems. FSx for Windows: integrates with Active Directory, supports DFS namespaces. FSx for Lustre: sub-millisecond latency for HPC, ML training. Can link to S3 for data repositories.

questions.question: What is AWS DataSync?
options: A managed database synchronization service that replicates RDS data across Regions
An RDS feature that synchronizes a primary database with read replicas in other Regions
A built-in DynamoDB feature that replicates tables across Regions in near real time
Accelerates online data transfer between on-premises storage, other clouds, and AWS storage
questions.explanation: DataSync automates and accelerates data migration/sync. Uses a DataSync Agent on-premises. Handles scheduling, monitoring, encryption, and data validation. Ideal for one-time migrations or ongoing data processing workflows.

questions.question: What is the AWS Shared Responsibility Model for Serverless (Lambda)?
options: The customer is responsible for each layer including the Lambda runtime and its OS patching
The customer handles OS patching while AWS handles the remaining layers of the Lambda stack
The split is identical to EC2: AWS owns the hypervisor and the customer owns the layers above
AWS handles infrastructure, OS, and runtime patching; customer handles code, IAM, data, and config
questions.explanation: Serverless shifts more responsibility to AWS. For Lambda, you don't manage: servers, OS, runtime patches, capacity. You still own: your code, IAM roles, data encryption, network access, and application-level security.

questions.question: What is Amazon Cognito?
options: A managed serverless NoSQL database that stores user profiles for web and mobile apps
A drop-in replacement for IAM that manages AWS console access for end customers
User authentication and authorization with User Pools (directories) and Identity Pools (federation)
A VPN authentication service that issues client certificates for AWS Client VPN access
questions.explanation: Cognito User Pools: user directory, handles sign-up/sign-in, MFA, OAuth2. Identity Pools (Federated Identities): swap tokens from social providers (Google, Facebook) or User Pools for temporary AWS credentials.

questions.question: What is AWS License Manager?
options: Manages BYOL software licenses across AWS and on-premises and helps avoid non-compliance
An AWS-operated software purchasing portal that resells third-party commercial software
A subscription manager that consolidates SaaS billing across AWS Marketplace vendors
A licensing tool that issues IAM permissions to users based on a license inventory
questions.explanation: License Manager helps track BYOL (Bring Your Own License) software deployments on EC2, prevents launching instances that would violate license terms, and provides a centralized dashboard for license inventory.

questions.question: What are AWS Availability Zones and why should applications use multiple AZs?
options: Availability Zones are naming labels for data centers and provide no failure isolation themselves
AZs share power and cooling so a single utility outage tends to affect each AZ at the same time
AZs are physically separate facilities with independent power and network; multi-AZ survives single-AZ failure
Deploying multi-AZ doubles a workload's monthly cost regardless of the architecture or workload
questions.explanation: Each AZ is one or more discrete data centers with redundant power/network. They're connected with low-latency links but isolated from each other's failures. Multi-AZ = high availability. ELB + Auto Scaling + RDS Multi-AZ = HA architecture.

questions.question: What is AWS Control Tower?
options: A console for managing physical data center inventory and rack-level capacity planning
A reporting service that produces SOC, PCI, and ISO compliance attestations for auditors
An IAM role lifecycle management service that creates, rotates, and audits assumed roles
Automates a multi-account Landing Zone with guardrails and an Account Factory for new accounts
questions.explanation: Control Tower builds a Landing Zone with: Log Archive account, Audit account, and an Account Factory. Guardrails (preventive = SCPs, detective = Config Rules) enforce compliance automatically across all accounts.

questions.question: Finance asks BI for monthly KPI dashboards over Athena/Redshift/RDS data, accessible in a browser, no servers to operate, with per-reader pricing. Which AWS service fits?
options: CloudWatch — operational metrics dashboards, NOT a BI tool over warehouses
Amazon QuickSight — serverless BI: dashboards over S3 / Redshift / Athena / RDS / databases, per-reader pricing
AWS Glue — ETL service, doesn't render BI dashboards
AWS CloudTrail — control-plane audit logs, not BI
questions.explanation: QuickSight connects to dozens of data sources and enables self-service BI with SPICE (in-memory computation engine). ML Insights adds anomaly detection and forecasting. Pay-per-session pricing model.

questions.question: A finance team compares EC2 cost models: (a) ~12 months of free usage on small instance types, (b) per-hour pay-as-you-go, (c) 1- or 3-year commitment with 40-72% discount, (d) interruptible spare capacity at up to 90% off. Which mapping is correct?
options: All four have the same effective hourly rate — false
Spot is dedicated long-running capacity — false, it is INTERRUPTIBLE
Reserved is more expensive than On-Demand — false, opposite
Free Tier = 12-month free for limited usage; On-Demand = pay-as-you-go; Reserved = 1/3-yr commit with big discount; Spot = interruptible spare capacity at deep discount
questions.explanation: EC2 pricing: On-Demand (full price, flexible), RI Standard (fixed type, ~72% off, 1-3yr), RI Convertible (~66% off, can change type), Spot (bid on spare capacity, cheapest, interruptible with 2-min notice), Savings Plans (flexible commitment).
